phase.label: Saint-Rémy, September 1889 — a repetition of an Arles composition

highlight.text: The shadows and the cast shadows are suppressed; it is painted in free flat tints like the Japanese prints.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 554 to Theo van Gogh, Arles, 16 October 1888
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

work.text: The composition exists in three versions, the first of which Van Gogh conceived in October 1888, a month after he moved into the home.

The painting in the Art Institute’s collection is Van Gogh’s second version of the scene, made nearly a year after the first, in September 1889. He produced a third, smaller version at the same time as a gift for his mother and sister.

moment.text: I'd like you to spend some time here, you'd feel it — after some time your vision changes, you see with a more Japanese eye, you feel colour differently.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 620 to Theo van Gogh, Arles, c. 5 June 1888

matters.text: This time it's just simply my bedroom, only here colour is to do everything, and giving by its simplification a grander style to things, is to be suggestive here of rest or of sleep in general. In a word, looking at the picture ought to rest the brain, or rather the imagination.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 554 to Theo van Gogh, Arles, 16 October 1888
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

matters.lead: Writing to Theo about the first version:

matters.text: This by way of revenge for the enforced rest I was obliged to take.
